beats.text: In 1957 the Sydney Opera House was budgeted at A$7 million.
beats.note: That was 3.5 million pounds. The planned completion date was 26 January 1963, Australia Day.

beats.context: The final cost in Australian dollars, nearly fifteen times the estimate. It opened on 20 October 1973, ten years after the planned date.

beats.note: He left the project on 28 February 1966 and never returned to Australia. He was invited to the opening and did not come.

beats.text: Psychologists call this the planning fallacy.
beats.note: Kahneman and Tversky first proposed it. It is the tendency to underestimate the time, costs and risks of future actions while overestimating the benefits.

beats.text: A 1994 study of 37 students found the same bias.
beats.note: They predicted 33.9 days on average to finish. The real average was 55.5 days, and only about 30 per cent finished on their predicted date.

beats.text: Your own deadline is probably optimistic too.
